why: Meshed gears must turn opposite ways, so this is 2-coloring the graph (bipartite check): BFS from gear 0 colouring neighbours with the opposite direction, and an edge between two same-coloured gears means an odd cycle, which locks the mechanism.
hints: Gear 0 is clockwise, so its neighbours are counterclockwise, their neighbours clockwise... What graph property makes this impossible?
This is a bipartite check. If an edge ever joins two gears that got the same direction, return [-1, -1].
BFS from 0 with side[v] in {0, 1}; on conflict stop. Otherwise count side 0 and side 1. O(n + edges).
pitfalls: Any odd cycle (like a triangle) locks the system.
A self-loop [u, u] is an immediate conflict.
Return counts in the order [clockwise, counterclockwise], with gear 0 clockwise.
